children.text: When Jane and Mr Bingley begin dancing, Mr Darcy and Elizabeth are left standing together at the side of the room. This leads to one of their more awkward interactions, where Mr Darcy refuses to dance with Elizabeth, despite their being a lack of men in the room (this is evidenced by a later clip where Elizabeth dances with Charlotte). Elizabeth seems rather hurt by his clipped response, especially after she was slightly delighted by his attention earlier. His coldness towards her contributes to the barrier of her believing he is unfeeling toward her.

Elizabeth overhears a conversation between Mr Bingley and Mr Darcy where Mr Darcy refers to her as "tolerable, but not handsome enough to tempt me" and she is offended. This contributes to the barrier, because Elizabeth struggles to forget his assessment of her, and her pride prevents her from ignoring it.
Charlotte and Jane mock Mr Darcy, and Jane decides he is the last man she would ever dance with. This becomes relevant when she says a similar thing to Mr Darcy during his proposal.
Mr Darcy broods in the corner while everyone else has a lovely time dancing. He doesn't tend to engage with society, which is another point against him in Elizabeth's books.
